abandon: m07 says the top directions of any GRPO-style RL-Zero delta write a reward-agnostic length prior that pulls every answer toward one target of a few thousand tokens, lengthening short answers and cutting long ones. The board already contradicts all three parts. (1) It is not reward-agnostic. The 8 directions of the General RL-Zero run, a GRPO run from the same recipe, do not finish answers: result-6f1bb7 reports 'General 164/88', i.e. 88 cap hits against the base's 77, where Math gives 46 and the dial goes down to 5. The whole IF delta also drives answers to almost no length, not to a few thousand tokens: result-edceef gives 'IF 55 (answers in a median of 5 tokens)'. The length these runs settle on depends on the reward. (2) There is no target of a few thousand tokens at which long answers are cut. In the item m07 starts from, result-1b6bf2, every quantile of finished length rises at 1x: 'top-8 1252/5513/14398 -> 1654/6094/14816', so p90 goes up, not down. For RL itself, 'RL 1295/6174/13532 -> 2401/7718/13532': p10 and p50 rise and p90 does not move. If there is a fixed point, it sits near 13-14k tokens, not between 2,500 and 8,000 as m07's first test requires. Only the 2x edit lowers p90 ('2x 1297/6409/14487 -> 2107/7088/12308'), and the 2x row is the over-dose regime. (3) The 'cuts long ones' half has no support other than cap hits being turned into finished answers. That is an end-of-answer effect, the additive hazard of m08, not a pull toward one length from both sides. So the same directions lengthen short answers and leave the tail in place or lengthen it.
